name: California

statute.name: California Public Records Act (CPRA)
statute.citation: Cal. Gov't Code § 7920.000 et seq. (disclosure at §§ 7922.510, 7922.530; suit at § 7923.000)

response.rule_text: Agency must make nonexempt records 'promptly' available, and has 10 days from receipt to determine whether the records are disclosable, Cal. Gov't Code §§ 7922.530(a), 7922.535(a).

fees.labor_rule: Only 'direct costs of duplication' (copy machine and operator time); staff search/review time not chargeable for paper records; data-extraction cost chargeable for electronic records, Cal. Gov't Code § 7922.530(a).
fees.copy_rule: Direct costs of duplication or statutory fee, § 7922.530(a).
fees.waiver_rule: CPRA contains no provision for fee waivers.

residency.rule_text: 'Every person' may inspect public records, Cal. Gov't Code § 7922.510.

appeal.body: Superior court (any court of competent jurisdiction)
appeal.rule_text: CPRA has no administrative appeal and allows immediate court action without exhaustion, Cal. Gov't Code § 7923.000; AG may not enforce unless the AG was itself denied. No statutory limitations period (general 3 years, Civ. Proc. Code § 338, may apply).

notes: Extension: 'unusual circumstances' add up to 14 days (10+14=24, per RCFP). Legislature excluded from CPRA (Gov't Code § 7920.510); covered instead by Legislative Open Records Act § 9070. Whether delay equals denial is only 'arguable' per RCFP, so null. Exemption citation, governor, universities, schools not extracted.
